intelligence.essence: A pull request is not work done — it is work *waiting*. Every merge you open is yours until it lands or is deliberately closed: check it through to completion, score it to the bar, and never let it pile up. Opened is not done. Land it, close it, or kill it — those are the only three endings.
intelligence.human_view:
Here is how a team drowns in its own good work. Someone builds something real, opens the merge, and says "I did it." But the merge never goes through — a check is red, a review never comes, something else gets louder — and it just sits there. Then another sits. Then hundreds pile up, each one a small lie that says progress happened when what actually happened was a *start*.

Shawn named the cure, and it is now law: **you must always check that your merge went through and completed.** If it needs a scorecard to reach ten out of ten, do the scorecard. If the merge no longer matters — because another solution won, or a newer merge replaced it — close the old one, deliberately, with the reason on it. There are no unleft merges. Ever. An open pull request is a promise with your name on it, and high-performance people finish their promises or formally release them. Nothing rots in the pile.
intelligence.simple_view: If you start building a tower, you don't walk away with the blocks half-stacked and say "done." You finish the tower — or you put the blocks back in the box and say why. Leaving towers half-built all over the floor isn't building. It's just a mess with your name on it.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like mailing a letter. Writing it isn't sending it. You check that it actually went — and if you decide not to send it after all, you don't leave it sitting on the counter for a year; you put it away on purpose. Work is the same: finish it, or file it away properly. Never just leave it lying there.
intelligence.naya_view: The Merge-Completion Law (Shawn, 2026-10-21 ~18:20Z), binding on every seat: (1) The author of a PR owns it until it is MERGED (with post-merge faithfulness proof) or CLOSED with a stated reason (superseded-by link / no longer needed / duplicate). (2) "I opened it" is never a completion report; completion claims cite the merge commit or the close. (3) Red gates on your PR are yours to diagnose: cure what's yours, name what's inherited (with its curing PR), request the different-seat scorecard — never leave red unexplained. (4) Supersession is an action, not an event: when a new solution replaces yours, YOU close the old PR the same hour. (5) The pile is audited: an open PR with no living owner and no path to the bar gets closed at triage, not carried forever. Today's specimen and cure, worked live in front of Shawn: PR #2850 (Smart Note Protocol) — created, then found sitting with 3 red checks and a stale body; diagnosed gate-by-gate (spec-integrity cured in-PR; doc-completeness red proven inherited from 0030, cure = PR #2852 (landed — merged 2026-10-21); consensus = different-seat scorecard requested), body refreshed, categorization law folded in — driven, not dropped.
intelligence.ai_view: A team's real velocity is measured at the merge, not at the opening. Every unleft merge is drag: it hides what's actually true, confuses the next seat, and turns "we did it" into a claim nobody can cash. A zero-pile team always knows exactly what is real — because everything it started is either landed and proven, or closed and explained.
